targetConcurrencyAndCompatibility.canonical: DELETE /adminapi/product/product/:id toggles; optional sole unique expected_is_del=0|1 verifies current source state; empty body only with finite UTF8 streaming bound.
targetConcurrencyAndCompatibility.aliasBehavior: Existing one-way recycle contract retained; already-deleted alias succeeds with no repeated cart/audit/outbox effects. Alias audit uses canonical path.
targetConcurrencyAndCompatibility.lockOrder: Live authority barriers -> no-lock full family snapshot <=10000 -> ascending every affected bargain exclusive -> every product try fence -> real store_product/SKU/cart/relation SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE NOWAIT barriers -> reread exact initial family -> row locks/readsets -> writes/full RETURNING -> business, complete audit/outbox sets -> final live authority -> final readbacks and database clock.
targetConcurrencyAndCompatibility.declaredTradeoff: Four table barriers briefly block unrelated business writes and require UPDATE privileges even on unchanged SKU/relation tables. Existing authority barriers require system_admin/system_role UPDATE; numeric legacy grants such as169 additionally require system_menus UPDATE for decision-time FOR SHARE. Capacity bounds and NOWAIT fail closed. Conflicts/new family members during the initial bargain wait cause409, rather than silently omitting a child. No order locks or order DML are used; normal independent order changes do not reject recycle.
targetConcurrencyAndCompatibility.durability: Business, canonical product_recycle DELETE audit and dedicated outbox commit atomically. Postcommit dispatch failure cannot turn a committed transition into a business failure; later Queue/outbox processing retries external effects.
targetConcurrencyAndCompatibility.transport: Canonical source toggle is relative and non-idempotent. Unknown network outcome must not be automatically resent; modern UI supplies explicit expected state and performs a fresh read.
